_doc: Seed for the rule_template DB catalog (loaded by catalog_store). This is VERSIONED DATA — the template contract metadata. The SQL builders that turn each template into DuckDB SQL stay in code (rule_compiler._BUILDERS), keyed by `name`. `field_params` is the declarative replacement for the old Python `fields` lambda: it tells the loader which params hold field names. engine is a vestigial legacy value (single DuckDB engine at runtime).

templates.name: required_field
templates.description: A field must be present and non-empty on every row.

templates.name: value_in_set
templates.description: A field's value must be one of an allowed set (enum). Optional `excluded` carves out values from that set in ONE rule (e.g. Territory: United States excluding Puerto Rico).

templates.name: value_not_in_set
templates.description: A field's value must NOT be one of an excluded set (exclusion).

templates.name: max_limit
templates.description: A numeric field must be <= max (optionally within a row scope).

templates.name: min_limit
templates.description: A numeric field must be >= min (optionally within a row scope).

templates.name: range_check
templates.description: A numeric field must be between min and max inclusive.

templates.name: pattern_check
templates.description: A field must match a regular expression.

templates.name: date_relation
templates.description: Two date fields in a row must satisfy field <op> other_field (op = compliant relation: <, <=, >, >=, =, !=).

templates.name: conditional_required
templates.description: If condition.field <op> condition.value, required_field must be present.

templates.name: conditional_value
templates.description: If condition.field <op> condition.value, the target field must satisfy field <op> value. Use for 'unless/except' value rules, e.g. 'unless Insured State = California, Paper must be Specialty'. op = <,<=,>,>=,=,!=.

templates.name: conditional_all
templates.description: MULTI-COLUMN condition: when ALL of `conditions` (a list of {field, op, value}) hold, the target field must satisfy field <op> value. Use when the requirement depends on TWO OR MORE columns at once, e.g. 'if <A> = <X> AND <B> = <Y> then <C> must be <Z>' -> conditions=[{field:<A>,op:'=',value:<X>},{field:<B>,op:'=',value:<Y>}], field:<C>, op:'=', value:<Z>. op = <,<=,>,>=,=,!=.

templates.name: period_duration
templates.description: datediff(unit, start_field, end_field) must satisfy a bound (unit = day|month|year). Use a RANGE with min and/or max when the duration has a lower and/or upper bound (e.g. min 12 and max 18 -> one rule, 12<=duration<=18); or a single op+value (op = compliant relation).

templates.name: aggregate_cap
templates.description: SUM/COUNT/DISTINCT_COUNT of a field, grouped, must stay within max/min (aggregation = sum|count|distinct_count).

templates.name: cross_field_math
templates.description: result_field must equal left_field <operator> right_field within tolerance_pct (operator = + - * /).

templates.name: cross_field_compare
templates.description: A numeric field compared (INEQUALITY allowed) to another field, optionally scaled by a constant: field <op> other_field [operator factor]. Use for 'Fronting Fee >= 12.5% of GWP' (field=Fronting Fee, op='>=', other_field=GWP, operator='*', factor=0.125) or 'Administrator fees <= Company fees' (field=Admin, op='<=', other_field=Company). op = <,<=,>,>=,=,!=; operator = + - * / (omit for a plain field-to-field compare).

templates.name: cross_field_or_value
templates.description: A numeric field compared to the GREATER (or LESSER) of a scaled other field OR a constant, in ONE rule: field <op> GREATEST/LEAST(other_field <operator> factor, value). Use for 'the greater of P% of B or $C' (bound=greater) or 'the lesser of P% of B or $C' (bound=lesser). e.g. 'Fronting Fee >= the greater of 12.5% of GWP or $15,000' -> field=Fronting Fee, op='>=', other_field=GWP, operator='*', factor=0.125, value=15000, bound='greater'. operator/factor optional.

templates.name: uniqueness
templates.description: The combination of fields must be unique across rows.

templates.name: date_bound
templates.description: A date field must satisfy field <op> a FIXED calendar date (op = <,<=,>,>=,=,!=; date = ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD'). Use for a contract/program PERIOD BOUNDARY that bounds every policy row: the program period is the SUPERSET and each policy period is a SUBSET of it, so a policy inception date must be >= the Program Inception/Effective/Commencement Date, and a policy expiry date must be <= the Program Expiration/Termination/End Date. Unlike date_relation (two columns) this compares ONE date column to a constant from the contract.

templates.name: cross_field_or_value
templates.description: A numeric field compared to the GREATER (or LESSER) of a scaled other field OR a constant, in ONE rule: field <op> GREATEST/LEAST(other_field <operator> factor, value). Use for 'the greater of P% of B or $C' (bound=greater) or 'the lesser of P% of B or $C' (bound=lesser) — a SINGLE combined bound, never a separate cross_field_compare + min/max pair. e.g. 'Fronting Fee >= the greater of 12.5% of GWP or $15,000' → field=Fronting Fee, op='>=', other_field=GWP, operator='*', factor=0.125, value=15000, bound='greater'. operator/factor optional (omit for a direct 'greater of B or C').
